title: Change permit (connector protocol 2.0, draft)
description: A single-use permit the Brain signs for one approved action of a change set (SPEC-write-back-21, GI-CONN-05). Knovas Link carries out an action only with a permit whose signature it verifies with a key it pinned from the Brain, that names its own tenant and site, the job's source, action, target and parameter hash, whose expiry has not passed and whose id it has not used. The signature covers the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of claims. A permit carries no credential and no value of the change: only the hash of the parameters. Closed.

alg.description: Ed25519 (RFC 8032) over the canonical JSON of claims.

kid.description: The id of the Brain's permit key, as GET /secured/connector/v2/permit-keys names it.

utc.description: UTC, whole seconds, with Z: one spelling, so the canonical JSON is one string.

permit_id.description: Single use. Also the idempotency key of the write: every repeat of a written permit is answered with its first result (SPEC-write-back-10).

tenant.description: The tenant of the approved change set; Link compares it with the tenant of its own certificate.

site.description: The site that holds the source's credential: Knovas Link's site id, as it declared it to the Brain. Only that site may claim the job, and Link refuses any other (SPEC-write-back-23).

action_id.description: The action of the change set this permit carries out.

action.description: The connector's action name (the declaration's), not the ontology's action type.

target.description: The item's external_id in the source.

params_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of the step's params object.

expected_version.description: The item's version the approved preview read. A source at another version is a conflict; nothing is written (SPEC-write-back-32).

expires_at.description: At most 60 minutes after issued_at. A first delivery after it is refused; a repeat of a permit written before it still gets its first result.

approved_by.description: The declared approver, recorded and never trusted for a decision until verified identity exists (SPEC-write-back-40, the identity gap).
